title: Respiratory System - February 2025 semester photo paper
note: Cover explicitly says February 2025 semester, 40 questions and 40 minutes. This does not establish an exact exam date. All nine images inspected; no option-specific answer marks are visible. Source spelling is retained with minimal whitespace/chemical-symbol normalization.

questions.prompt: All the following bones are involved in the formation of the posterior opening (choana) of the nose except...
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The choana is bounded by vomer, palatine and sphenoid; maxilla is not a boundary.

questions.prompt: Which of the following arteries branches from the Maxillary artery, which is a branch of the external carotid?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Sphenopalatine is a terminal maxillary branch; ethmoidal arteries arise from ophthalmic and superior labial from facial.

questions.prompt: Which of the following options are correct?
options: The ethmoidal bulla is located at a lower level than the inferior concha.
The maxillary sinus open to the Semilunar hiatus.
The nasolacrimal duct open to the middle meatus.
The group of middle Ethmoidal cells opens to the superior meatus.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Maxillary sinus drains through the semilunar hiatus into the middle meatus. Nasolacrimal drainage is inferior; middle ethmoidal cells drain onto the bulla in the middle meatus.

questions.prompt: All the following structures are adjacent to medial surface of right lung except...?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The usual named right mediastinal impressions include azygos arch and venae cavae; thoracic duct is not a direct named right-lung impression. Final two options continue on source image 3.

questions.prompt: Which of the following options are characteristics of the parietal plura?
options: It is innervated by sympathic nerves.
It penetrate into the grooves of the lung.
The lower end of the parietal plura in the mid clavicular line, is at the level of the 8th rib.
Visceral plura is going to form pulmonary ligament.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Parietal pleura reaches rib 8 in the midclavicular line. Its somatic sensation and lack of entry into lung fissures distinguish it from visceral pleura.

questions.prompt: All the following options are correct except...?
options: Right bronchus is thicker than the left main broncus.
Right bronchus is shorter than the left main bronchus.
Left main bronchus compare to right main bronchus, is farther from the midline
Left main bronchus Before penetrating the umbilicus of the right lung, is divided
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The left main bronchus enters the left lung, not the right. The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statment is false?
options: The upper edge of the quadrangular membrane form aryepiglottic fold
Aryepiglotic fold participate in forming of inlet of larynx.
False vocal fold anteriorly attached to the arythnoid cartilage.
The upper side of the cricothyroid memberane (or conus elasticus) makes true vocal folds.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The vestibular fold attaches anteriorly to thyroid and posteriorly to arytenoid; C reverses the orientation.

questions.prompt: All of the following are true in relation to the internal laryngeal nerve except:
options: It provides the sensation of the laryngeal mucosa above the real vocal folds.
It is one of the two terminal branches of the superior laryngeal nerve.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Internal laryngeal is predominantly sensory above the vocal folds; intrinsic motor supply is recurrent laryngeal except cricothyroid via external laryngeal.

questions.prompt: Vocal muscle is part of which of the muscles of the larynx?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Vocalis is the medial specialized portion of thyroarytenoid.

questions.prompt: Contraction of which muscle causes the true vocal folds to abdduct?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Posterior cricoarytenoid abducts the vocal folds.

questions.prompt: Which of the laryngeal muscles is going to innervate by external laryngeal nerve?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: External laryngeal motor fibers supply cricothyroid.

questions.prompt: Which nerve passes through the incisive fossa?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Nasopalatine traverses the incisive canal opening into the incisive fossa.

questions.prompt: The respiratory diverticulum originates from which of the following structures?
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: Foregut is the anatomical structure from whose ventral wall the diverticulum buds. Endoderm correctly names its epithelial germ-layer lineage, so the wording mixes levels of description; B is the best structural answer. Options C-D continue on image 5.

questions.prompt: In which stages does the primary alveole arise?
options: Terminal sac stage (24-26 weeks to birth)
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: The terminal-sac/saccular period forms primitive alveoli or terminal sacs; mature alveolar development continues in the alveolar period.

questions.prompt: In microscopic structure Which part of the Air duct is observed Erectile Tissue?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The characteristic venous erectile plexuses belong to respiratory mucosa over the nasal conchae. That site is not offered; none of the listed regions is an unambiguous substitute.

questions.prompt: In microscopic structure Which part of air duct of respiratory system is observed Elastic Fiber and Elastic Cartilage?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The epiglottis has an elastic-cartilage core with elastic connective tissue; bronchial cartilage is hyaline.

questions.prompt: In microscopic structure which part of lobules Lung Tissue is observed simple Esquamose Cell epithelial Tissue?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Alveoli and alveolar openings bordering ducts have squamous type I epithelium, while respiratory bronchioles also contain alveolar interruptions. Both A and D are defensible; no unique answer. D continues on image 6.

questions.prompt: In microscopic structure Of lung tissue, which part of these system is observed pneumocytes type III?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Visual review confirms III, not II. The source likely uses an obsolete/nonstandard label for alveolar macrophages; the course review distinguishes macrophages from pneumocytes. No validated answer is assigned to this terminology.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following increases the volume of the thoracic cage?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Scalene contraction elevates upper ribs and assists inspiration. The ordinary exam comparison treats internal intercostals as expiratory; their interchondral portion has a different action.

questions.prompt: What is the normal alveolar pressure (cmH2O) at the beginning and end of normal expiration, respectively?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At the exact no-flow transitions, alveolar pressure equals atmospheric pressure (zero gauge); it becomes positive during expiratory flow.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following leads to an increase in diameter of airways?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Sympathoadrenal beta-2 effects dilate bronchioles, whereas cholinergic vagal and histamine effects constrict them. Direct sympathetic airway innervation is relatively sparse.

questions.prompt: If the tidal volume is 450 ml for a change in transpulmonary pressure of 3 cmH2O, how much will the lung compliance be?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Compliance equals change in volume divided by change in pressure: 450/3 = 150 mL/cmH2O.

questions.prompt: What is the "residual Volume"?
options: The volume of air remaining in the lungs after the most forceful expiration
The maximum amount of air a person can expel from the lungs after first filling the lungs to their maximum extent
The amount of air that remains in the lungs at the end of normal expiration
The extra volume of air that can be expired by deep exhalation
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Residual volume remains after maximal expiration. Options B-D continue on image 7.

questions.prompt: Which zone of the lungs has continuous blood flow in an upright lung in rest?
options: Zone-III at the bottom of the lung
Zone-II at the top of the lung
Zone-III at the top of the lung
Zone-II at the bottom of the lung
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Dependent lung typically has zone-3 conditions with both arterial and venous pressures above alveolar pressure, allowing continuous flow.

questions.prompt: In normal condition, what is the O2 pressure at the end of pulmonary capillary?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: End-pulmonary-capillary blood equilibrates with alveolar PO2 around 104 mmHg in the reference model; systemic arterial PO2 is lower after venous admixture.

questions.prompt: What is the hypoxia-induced vasoconstriction mechanism?
options: A decrease in alveolar oxygen pressure to less than 60 mm Hg causes increased blood flow in the pulmonary capillaries.
A decrease in alveolar oxygen pressure to less than 73 mm Hg causes decreased blood flow in the pulmonary capillaries.
A decrease in alveolar oxygen pressure to less than 104 mm Hg causes decreased blood flow in the pulmonary capillaries.
A decrease in alveolar oxygen pressure to less than 73 mm Hg causes increased blood flow in the pulmonary capillaries.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: B matches the textbook threshold comparison (roughly 70% of normal alveolar PO2) and direction: low alveolar oxygen raises local vascular resistance and reduces flow. The 73 mmHg value is a teaching approximation, not a universal threshold.

questions.prompt: What happens to the rate of CO2 diffusion when the respiratory membrane If the thickness of the respiratory membrane increases threefold due to lung fibrosis?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Diffusion rate varies inversely with thickness when other factors remain fixed, so tripling thickness reduces rate to one third. Duplicated phrase is printed in the source.

questions.prompt: Activation of which one of the following centers can increase respiratory rate?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Stronger pontine pneumotaxic switch-off shortens inspiration and tends to raise breathing frequency in the teaching model.

questions.prompt: What is the main factor that can indirectly lead to central chemoreceptor stimulation?
options: An increase in hydrogen ion concentration in the blood
An increase in Carbon Monoxide (CO) pressure in the blood
An increase in Carbon dioxide (CO2) pressure in the blood
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Blood CO2 crosses into brain extracellular fluid/CSF and generates H+ that stimulates central chemoreceptors.

questions.prompt: Which ion has a less concentration in RBCs of arterial blood than blood venous?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Cl- is the intended reverse-chloride-shift comparison, but higher venous PCO2 also changes intracellular bicarbonate and H+. The stem does not isolate the exchanged ion and has more than one physiologically defensible answer.

questions.prompt: What condition causes a physiological shunt?
options: A decrease in ventilation/perfusion ratio (VA/Q) to 0.6 at the top of the upright lung
Mixture of pulmonary vein blood with bronchial vein blood
An increase in VA/Q ratio to 2.5 at the bottom of the upright lung
A decrease in ventilation/perfusion ratio (V/Q) to 0.6 at the bottom of the upright lung
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: B gives anatomical venous admixture, while low-V/Q perfusion also contributes to physiological shunt calculations (D, and a hypothetical low-V/Q apex in A). The source wording does not support a unique answer.

questions.prompt: Which one is correct about the oxygen utilization coefficient?
options: It increases only to twice during heavy exercise.
It can triple during heavy exercise.
At rest, its normal level is 40%.
With an increase in the body's metabolism, the amount of it decreases.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Extraction can rise from about 25% at rest to about 75% during heavy exercise, a threefold increase.

questions.prompt: What factor increases lung compliance?
options: An increase in the amount of elastin and collagen in the lung parenchyma
A decrease in the amount of surface tension
Removing the surfactant from alveolar fluid layer
An increase in lung elastic forces
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Lower surface tension reduces recoil and makes the lung more compliant.

questions.prompt: An increase in which factor causes a left shift in the hemoglobin-oxygen dissociation curve?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Increased pH increases oxygen affinity and shifts the curve left.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is NOT a part of respiratory membrane?
options: A fluid layer of water and surfactants covering the luminal surface of alveolar cells
Basement membranes of endothelial and alveolar cells
Smooth muscle cells surrounding the endothelial cells
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: A smooth-muscle layer is not part of the thin alveolar-capillary gas-exchange barrier.

questions.prompt: If the diffusing capacity of O2 is 15 ml/min/mmHg in a patient, how much will the CO2 diffusing capacity be?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Using the textbook approximate CO2:O2 diffusion ratio of 20, 15 x 20 = 300 mL/min/mmHg.

questions.prompt: Which of the following occur during normal inspiration?
options: Phrenic nerves are inhibited, pleural pressure decreases, alveolar pressure increases
Phrenic nerves are activated, pleural pressure decreases, alveolar pressure decreases
Phrenic nerves are activated, pleural pressure increases, alveolar pressure increases
Diaphragm contracts, pleural pressure increases, alveolar pressure decreases
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Phrenic activation contracts the diaphragm; pleural pressure becomes more negative and alveolar pressure transiently falls during inspiratory flow. Options B-D continue on image 9.

questions.prompt: Which one the following is CORRECT about pulmonary surfactant?
options: Thyroid hormone leads to an increase in surfactant
It is produced in type I alveolar cells
Most of its composition is related to proteins
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Thyroid hormone can stimulate fetal surfactant phospholipid synthesis; type II cells produce lipid-rich surfactant. Primary experimental support is cited; this is a developmental mechanism, not a treatment recommendation.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following factors has no effect on distribution of pulmonary blood flow in different zones of the lung?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: C is the intended West-zone comparison: vascular/alveolar pressures, gravity and exercise determine the zones directly. The absolute no effect wording overlooks possible indirect surface-tension effects.

questions.prompt: Which respiratory center provides action potential for contraction of diaphragm during normal inspiration?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: DRG is the expected traditional exam answer for quiet inspiratory drive to phrenic motor pathways; modern respiratory control involves interacting medullary networks.

excludedItems.reason: Exam cover and directions only; confirms 40 MCQs and February 2025 semester.

audit.notes: All preferred source images visually reviewed; OCR used only as a drafting aid. All supplied complete items retained. Source annotations are unofficial, preserved separately from the audited answer. Null audited keys deliberately quarantine ambiguous or defective questions. Numbered options 1-4 and Persian letters are normalized to A-D in displayed order.
